clue.text: Old king whose laws protect what uniform stands for

indicators.note: the laws protect, i.e. wrap around, the uniform's letter

parts.note: lois is French for laws
Uniform is the NATO alphabet code word for the letter U

explanation.surface: A historical monarch whose legal code safeguards the meaning of military dress.
explanation.definitionFit: Several French monarchs bore this name, so an old king of France fits.

clue.text: Pole, light-headed with malt, pops out

indicators.note: out signals the letters of the two words are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone dizzy from malt whisky passes out against a post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light-headed' looks like a description of a drunk, but with 'Pole' it defines: a street pole with a lamp at its head.
explanation.definitionFit: A street-lighting post is a pole whose top carries a lamp, a playful description.

clue.text: Like virgin reserves right to leave free?

indicators.note: the letter for right is told to depart from the word for free

parts.note: an animal that is free has not been caught, untrapped

explanation.surface: A question about whether untouched reserves are free once the right to exit is granted.
explanation.definitionFit: Virgin oil or mineral reserves have not yet been drawn on or exploited.

clue.text: Pledge total information blackout

parts.note: security is something pledged as a guarantee for a loan
blanket means all-covering, total, as in a blanket ban

explanation.surface: A promise of a complete news blackout.
explanation.definitionFit: A security blanket is an official ban on releasing information, usually for safety reasons.

clue.text: Works lacking a certain character

parts.note: pieces of writing composed deliberately without ever using one particular letter of the alphabet, character meaning letter

explanation.surface: Literary works with no personality.
explanation.definitionFit: These are texts written avoiding one letter throughout, such as a novel with no letter E.

clue.text: Bird left animal shelter

parts.note: Noah's ark sheltered the animals from the flood

explanation.surface: A bird has departed from a refuge for creatures.
explanation.definitionFit: The skylark is a songbird famous for singing in flight.

clue.text: Shrub flourishing is in teapot

indicators.note: flourishing, as in waving about with a flourish, signals the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A thriving plant is growing inside a teapot.
explanation.definitionFit: The red-bracted Christmas plant is a Mexican shrub of the spurge family.

clue.text: Populist government that's sensible to introduce in waves

indicators.note: one word is to be put into the middle of the other

parts.note: waves of the hand are gestures
politic means prudent or sensible, as in a politic decision

explanation.surface: A populist regime that thinks it wise to bring in reforms in successive waves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Waves' reads as surges of change, but it is the noun for hand movements; 'to introduce in' tells you where the sensible word goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Gesture politics means action done for show to win popular approval rather than for real effect.

clue.text: Airline agree to drop letters regularly in French department

indicators.note: every other letter is thrown out, leaving the first, third, fifth and so on

explanation.surface: An airline agrees to make regular mail drops in a region of France.
explanation.definitionFit: Ariège is a department of southern France in the Pyrenees.

clue.text: Slashes, therefore one hides under cover

indicators.note: in a down clue the letter for one sits below the cover, as if hiding beneath it

parts.note: so means therefore, as in so it follows
a lid is a cover
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone slashed, so one hides under the covers.
explanation.walkthrough: Slashes are the oblique strokes in printing, also called solidi.
explanation.definitionFit: The printed oblique stroke is called a solidus, plural solidi, also a slash.

clue.text: Came to fine after swallowing fish bones

parts.note: met means came together, converged at a meeting point

indicators.note: the word for fine comes next, with the fish taken inside it

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, fine, with the 1 read as I
a carp is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: Someone came round to a penalty after a fish dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 (first class) is written AI, the figure 1 standing as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Metacarpals are the hand bones between wrist and fingers.

clue.text: Sound from pipes in S-bend heard

indicators.note: heard signals that the letters are said aloud

parts.note: a bend shaped like an S is an S-curl

explanation.surface: A gurgling noise in the plumbing's U-shaped trap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pipes' suggests plumbing, but it is bagpipes; S-curl spoken sounds like their shrill wail.
explanation.definitionFit: A skirl is the shrill wailing sound made by bagpipes.

clue.text: Drivel, you rightly infer, starts as writer's out-of-date material

parts.note: pap is worthless, insipid talk or writing

indicators.note: the first letters of the following three words are taken

explanation.surface: A remark about nonsense being inferred from old documents.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancient scribes wrote on papyrus, a writing material long since obsolete.

clue.text: Satisfied with a return treat for magnetic effect

indicators.note: return signals the following word is read backwards

parts.note: to degauss is to treat something to remove its magnetism

explanation.surface: Content with a reward given in return for magnetic influence.
explanation.definitionFit: Assuaged means appeased or satisfied, as with hunger or thirst.

clue.text: Old interrogator raised a barrier with force

parts.note: torque is turning force

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means the letters are read upwards, backwards

parts.note: taken as written
a dam is a barrier across water

explanation.surface: An interrogator of old put up a barricade forcefully.
explanation.definitionFit: Tomás de Torquemada was the notorious Grand Inquisitor of the Spanish Inquisition.

clue.text: Inclined to put away unsavoury items?

definitions.text: Inclined to put away unsavoury items?

parts.words: Inclined to put away unsavoury items
parts.note: someone disposed to eat, put away, things that are not savoury, i.e. sweet things

explanation.surface: Someone tending to tidy away distasteful objects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put away' suggests tidying and 'unsavoury' suggests unpleasant, but they mean eating and sugary.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a liking for sweet food means preferring the unsavoury, sugary side.

clue.text: I pierced this rough fellow in the neck

indicators.note: rough signals the word this is roughed up, rearranged
the letter I goes into the word for fellow

parts.note: man is a fellow

explanation.surface: A violent confession of stabbing a rough fellow in the neck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rough' makes ISTH from 'this'; 'in the neck' sounds like the wound, but defines: relating to an isthmus, a neck of land.
explanation.definitionFit: An isthmus is a narrow neck of land, so the adjective describes things located in such a neck.

clue.text: Maid said, for example, to be shy?

definitions.meaning: the two words look as if they rhyme on the page but do not when spoken
punning reading: shy rhymes with eye, so being shy is to be a rhyme of the eye

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is a pun: a word rhyming with 'eye', such as 'shy', is a rhyme of that kind.
explanation.definitionFit: This term names a pair of words spelt alike at the end but pronounced differently.

clue.text: University developed by 1 ac about to finish globally

indicators.note: about signals the letters are turned around and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
the answer to 1 Across, the old king's name
to quit is to finish or stop

explanation.surface: A university founded by an old king is about to close worldwide.
explanation.definitionFit: Being everywhere at once is ubiquity, so this adverb means all over, globally.

clue.text: It might accommodate Arab firm

definitions.meaning: a building for horses could house an Arab, a breed of horse

explanation.walkthrough: 'Arab' is a horse breed, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse's building houses an Arab horse, and steady means firm.

clue.text: Sun, maybe, glowing over peak

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece is placed above the other

parts.note: red-hot things glow red
a top is a peak or summit

explanation.surface: The sun glowing above a mountain summit.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper; red-tops are tabloids with red mastheads.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sun is an example of a British tabloid with a red masthead.

clue.text: Literary bird that almost never flies

indicators.note: flies signals the letters scatter into a new order
almost means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A bird from literature that hardly ever takes flight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims 'that' to THA; 'flies' shuffles THA with NEVER.
explanation.definitionFit: Poe's poem features a famous talking bird that croaks Nevermore.

clue.text: Spot girl bringing instrument

parts.note: a zit is a pimple, a spot
her refers to a girl

explanation.surface: A spotty girl brings along a musical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A zither is a stringed instrument played flat, plucked with the fingers.

clue.text: Mock Jack, cross falling from goat

parts.note: J is the card abbreviation for jack

indicators.note: the cross drops out of the goat's name

parts.note: an ibex is a wild mountain goat
X is the shape of a cross

explanation.surface: Mocking Jack, an angry person falls off a goat.
explanation.definitionFit: To jibe is to taunt or mock someone.

clue.text: Method of colouring clothes sailor brought from east

indicators.note: in an across clue coming from the east means read right to left, backwards

parts.note: kit is clothing, as in football kit
AB, able seaman, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor brought back dyed clothes from the Orient.
explanation.definitionFit: Batik is a wax-resist technique of dyeing cloth, from Java.

clue.text: Idiocy of a Conservative forsaking urban crime?

indicators.note: the letter for Conservative is abandoned, dropped

parts.note: a sin in a city is an urban crime

explanation.surface: A Tory politician's foolishness in giving up on city crime.
explanation.definitionFit: Asininity is donkey-like stupidity, i.e. idiocy.

clue.text: Make detailed speech, getting exile worried on island

indicators.note: in an across clue on means placed after

parts.note: an expat lives in exile from home
ate means worried, as in what's eating you?

explanation.surface: Someone talking at length about an exile fretting on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: To expatiate is to speak or write at length in detail.

clue.text: Loudly celebrate creator of Playboy character

indicators.note: loudly means said out loud, a sound-alike

parts.note: to sing is to celebrate in song

explanation.surface: Loud celebration of the man behind a magazine figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Playboy' suggests the magazine, but it is The Playboy of the Western World, an Irish play.
explanation.definitionFit: J. M. Synge was the Irish playwright who created Christy Mahon in his famous comedy.
